records.why: KICD core competencies for this sub-strand are critical thinking and problem solving, self-efficacy, digital literacy, and communication and collaboration. The data listed 'Learning to learn' instead of self-efficacy. Each is tied to an activity in the lessons.
records.value:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: learners compare two sets of marks, analyse the evidence and use histograms, frequency polygons and other summaries to examine the data and justify predictions about next steps for learners and teachers.
• Self-Efficacy: learners discuss the meaning of the term data with peers, explore where data come from and gain confidence by predicting, checking and revising their statistical model as new measures and representations are introduced.
• Digital literacy: learners may use digital devices (calculators, or a spreadsheet or phone app where available) to draw and check histograms and frequency polygons.
• Communication and collaboration: learners discuss and defend their interpretations of the data in groups and present and share findings with different groups, such as school administrators, parents or community leaders.
records.reference: KICD Grade 10 curriculum design, Mathematics, Strand 3.0 Statistics and Probability, Sub-Strand 3.1 Statistics I

records.why: KICD values for this sub-strand are integrity, unity and love; the data had 'responsibility' instead of 'love'. The love value is tied to the no-blame rule already used in every lesson.
records.value:
• Integrity: learners record and report data accurately and honestly without altering scores.
• Unity: learners work in groups and use the data to draw histograms and frequency polygons and to interpret the data together.
• Love: learners are considerate of one another when they discuss the scores in pairs and groups, treating the scores as information about a test and never as a judgement of any learner or teacher.

records.why: Continues the language support from Lesson 2 for the three measures. Median and mode terms deliberately not supplied because they could not be verified.

records.new: Language support: add the new words to the board with Kiswahili beside them where the class agrees on a term (mean/wastani; agree terms for median, mode and 'middle' with the Kiswahili teacher) and allow pair discussion in Kiswahili before learners answer in English. Use the Kenyan side example

records.why: The lesson has a heavy fine-motor drawing task and no accommodation for learners with special needs or more than one way to show understanding (guideline 12). The spreadsheet check ties to the KICD core competency 'digital literacy' that was listed but not used in any activity. Kept short and optional because devices are not guaranteed.
records.old: Remind: 'Same scales for both subjects, or the comparison is not fair.'
records.new: Remind: 'Same scales for both subjects, or the comparison is not fair.' Supports and options: give learners who find drawing difficult pre-drawn axes or graph paper with larger squares and let a partner be the plotter; learners may show their understanding by explaining the graph aloud to you instead of writing, or by building the bars from cut strips of paper. Where a computer or phone is available, a group may check its histogram in a spreadsheet.

records.why: The mandazi 'fair share' analogy for the mean is used without saying where it stops. One sentence now states the limit, using the extreme-score question already in the lesson.
records.old: Do NOT introduce grouped-data formulas
records.new: State the limit of the 'fair share' picture: it explains the mean (everyone gets the same), but the median and mode are not shares, and one very high or very low score can drag the mean. Do NOT introduce grouped-data formulas

records.why: The rubric descriptors did not name the CBE levels, so a teacher reading the printed headings could not tell how they map to Exceeds, Meets and Approaches Expectations. Level names now start each descriptor. The 'Key Inquiry 1' label in the first criterion was removed because the KICD key inquiry questions were corrected (group G7); IQR values match Lesson 7.

value.excellent: Exceeds expectations: builds a complete, correct grouped table with a common class width of 10, correct tallies and frequencies totalling 20 for each subject, and clearly explains why grouping is more useful than an ungrouped table.
value.proficient: Meets expectations: builds a mostly correct table with one small error, and gives a basic reason for using the same classes or for grouping.
value.developing: Approaches expectations: table has several errors or totals that do not equal 20, or gives no reason for the choice of classes; needs help to complete the table.

value.criterion: Calculating measures (mean, median, mode, quartiles, IQR)
value.excellent: Exceeds expectations: all measures are correct (80.35, 80.5, 33.85, 31.5, modes 32 and 60, IQR estimates 13.2 and 24.2) with clear working, and grouped values are called estimates with a reason given.
value.proficient: Meets expectations: most measures are correct with working shown, with a small slip, or the reason for 'estimate' is incomplete.
value.developing: Approaches expectations: several measures are incorrect or working is missing, and the learner does not recognise grouped values as estimates.

value.excellent: Exceeds expectations: uses centre, spread, shape and pass rate together to compare the subjects, and explains what the graphs show that the raw lists hid.
value.proficient: Meets expectations: uses at least two features (such as the mean and the pass count) to compare the subjects, with limited reference to spread or shape.
value.developing: Approaches expectations: only lists numbers or describes one subject, with no comparison.

value.excellent: Exceeds expectations: gives a clear claim supported by several correct pieces of evidence, with reasoning that links them, and recommendations for Mr. Otieno, Mrs. Wanjiku, the learners and the 16 learners below 50, each linked to the data.
value.proficient: Meets expectations: gives a claim with some evidence and recommendations for most groups, but the link between the data and the recommendation is sometimes weak.
value.developing: Approaches expectations: claim is unsupported or recommendations are missing or not linked to the data.

value.criterion: Separating what the data shows from what it cannot explain
value.excellent: Exceeds expectations: treats reasons for the score difference as hypotheses using words such as 'may' and 'could', and names suitable extra data (topic-by-topic marks, a second test).
value.proficient: Meets expectations: recognises that causes are not known but gives an unclear or incomplete plan for finding out.
value.developing: Approaches expectations: states a cause for the score difference as a fact, or needs prompting to see that the data cannot show the cause.

records.why: The contract allows only three level fields (excellent, proficient, developing), so the fourth CBE level, Below Expectations, cannot be represented in this Final Explanation rubric. Suggestion: teachers use the Approaches descriptor plus their own note for Below Expectations until the contract adds a fourth level.

Strand and sub-strand numbering does not match KICD. The data call this 'Strand 4.0: Statistics and Probability, Sub-Strand 4.1: Statistics I'; the KICD Grade 10 Mathematics design (March 2025) numbers it Strand 3.0, Sub-Strand 3.1 Statistics I (16 lessons). Not renamed, as instructed; teachers should confirm which numbering the school and partner use.
records.reference: KICD Grade 10 curriculum design, Mathematics, Strand 3.0 Statistics and Probability, Sub-Strand 3.1 Statistics I

records.why: KICD content not fully taught: (1) histograms with UNEQUAL class widths (KICD lists equal and unequal) are not covered; (2) the KICD Project (collect, organise and present data from a school or community situation) is not included; (3) collecting data is only covered by the Lesson 2 homework added in this revision. Also, Lesson 7 teaches cumulative frequency, ogives, quartiles and the interquartile range, which are NOT in the KICD content or outcomes for this sub-strand; they are kept because the teachers built the lesson, but teachers should decide whether to keep Lesson 7 or replace it with unequal-width histograms and the project.
records.reference: KICD Grade 10 curriculum design, Mathematics, Strand 3.0 Statistics and Probability, Sub-Strand 3.1 Statistics I
